data.title: Updates to the Board of Directors of Ecopetrol S.A.
data.description:
BOGOTÁ, Colombia, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ecopetrol S.A. (; ) (the "Company") announces that, through a communication dated September 14, 2026, Mr. Hildebrando Vélez Galeano expressed his intention to resign from his position as a member of the Board of Directors, effective September 15, 2026.

Ecopetrol thanks Mr. Vélez Galeano for his contributions to the Board of Directors during his tenure, particularly his leadership and contributions on environmental matters and his continued commitment to strengthening the Company's relationship with local communities and regions. The Company also wishes him every success in his personal and professional endeavors.

Pursuant to the provisions of Ecopetrol's By-laws, the Board of Directors will continue to validly deliberate and adopt decisions with its remaining members.

Ecopetrol is the largest company in Colombia and one of the main integrated energy companies in the American continent, with more than 19,000 employees. In Colombia, it is responsible for more than 60% of the hydrocarbon production of most transportation, logistics, and hydrocarbon refining systems, and it holds leading positions in the petrochemicals and gas distribution segments. With the acquisition of 51.4% of ISA's shares, the company participates in energy transmission, the management of real-time systems (XM), and the Barranquilla–Cartagena coastal highway concession. At the international level, Ecopetrol has a stake in strategic basins in the American continent, with drilling and exploration operations in the United States (Permian basin and the Gulf of Mexico), Brazil, and Mexico, and, through ISA and its subsidiaries, Ecopetrol holds leading positions in the power transmission business in Brazil, Chile, Peru, and Bolivia, road concessions in Chile, and the telecommunications sector.

All forward-looking statements, whether made in this release or in future filings or press releases, or orally, address matters that involve risks and uncertainties, including in respect of the Company's prospects for growth and its ongoing access to capital to fund the Company's business plan, among others. data.title: Italian Antitrust Probes Intesa Sanpaolo's Bid for Monte dei Paschi
data.description:
By Mauro Orru

Italy's competition watchdog said it had launched an investigation into Intesa Sanpaolo's $35 billion bid for Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena.

The Italian Competition Authority said it wanted to assess how a potential deal could affect competition across the country's banking and insurance markets.

Intesa and Monte dei Paschi didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

Monte dei Paschi in June became the target of a cash-and-stock bid from Intesa. Monte dei Paschi said last month that it was weighing options to preserve its integrity.

data.title: London shares slip as higher oil prices lift bond yields; BoE in focus
data.description:
London shares slipped on Tuesday, hovering around two-month lows, as rising oil prices prompted a fresh rise in bond yields, while investors assessed domestic economic data ahead of a Bank of England monetary policy meeting later this week.

The blue-chip FTSE 100 index CURRENCYCOM:UK100 fell 0.4% to 10,658.13 points, while the midcap FTSE 250 slipped 0.1% to 23,818.74 points.

  • Oil prices , rose 2% after attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure raised supply concerns, in turn lifting shares of Shell and BP .

  • Major banks (.FTNMX301010), investment banks and brokerages (.FTNMX302020) were the top fallers with HSBC down 2.2% and Barclays 1.7% lower.

  • U.S. banks came under pressure for a second day after Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan said on Monday he expects investment banking fees to drop by at least 10% in the third quarter, and sales and trading revenue to be flat.

  • Global bond yields soared, with the UK 30-year gilt yield (GB30YT=RR) touching its highest since 1998 at 5.40%, as investors bet that rising oil prices could prompt central bank interest rate rises.

  • A report said that the BoE is poised to announce this week that it will stop selling 20- and 30-year gilts, potentially freeing up some cash for finance minister John Healey.

  • Britain's jobs market stayed weak in the third quarter, while a separate report showed grocery price inflation increased to 2.3% over the four weeks to September 6. Official data on inflation is due on Wednesday.

  • Traders see the BoE leaving interest rates unchanged at its monetary policy meeting, but still see rates rising by at least 48 basis points by year-end, LSEG-compiled data showed.

  • Wickes Group gained 8.3% after the home improvement retailer reported strong third-quarter trading, driven by mid-single-digit growth in retail like-for-like revenue.

  • Online reviews platform Trustpilot's shares plummeted 18.6% as its decision to leave its earnings outlook unchanged disappointed investors.

data.title: RTX CEO sees defense, aerospace demand supporting cash-flow growth
data.description:
RTX Chairman and Chief Executive Chris Calio on Tuesday said strong demand for air travel and rising global defense spending should support the aerospace and defense company’s growth for years, while increased factory automation and long-term military contracts help address production constraints.

Speaking with Morgan Stanley analyst Christine Liwag at the firm’s 14th Annual Laguna Conference, Calio said airlines continue to need newer, more fuel-efficient aircraft. He also pointed to heightened geopolitical threats that are prompting countries to increase defense spending and strengthen their domestic security capabilities.

For investors, Calio’s comments highlighted the breadth of RTX’s exposure to two durable markets. Its commercial aerospace businesses stand to benefit from rising aircraft production and aftermarket demand, while Raytheon is positioned for spending on missiles, radar systems and layered air defense. The principal challenge is execution, including expanding capacity and ensuring that suppliers can keep pace.

Defense backlog leaves room for additional awards

RTX has a backlog of about $289 billion, according to Calio. That figure does not include five framework agreements covering major munitions programs or a recently awarded seven-year, $23 billion Tomahawk contract.

Volumes under the five agreements could rise by two to four times, Calio said. Their multiyear structure gives RTX and its suppliers greater confidence to invest in equipment, facilities and employees.

That visibility is particularly important because about half of the company’s supply chain consists of small and midsize businesses. Some suppliers have been reluctant or unable to add capacity without firm orders extending beyond the government’s traditional annual procurement cycle.

Raytheon spans multiple layers of missile defense

Calio said Raytheon operates “right at the heart” of integrated air and missile defense. Sensors and effectors account for about 70% of the unit’s sales.

Its portfolio includes the Coyote counter-drone system, NASAMS, Patriot, the LTAMDS radar, SPY-6 naval radar and the Standard Missile family. Coyote has recorded more than 600 drone defeats in operational settings, Calio said. Raytheon also is developing a reusable, non-kinetic version that employs high-powered microwaves against drone swarms.

RTX expects demand for sophisticated weapons to remain strong even as the Pentagon seeks cheaper systems that can be manufactured in larger numbers. Calio described the market as an “and, not an or,” with lower-cost weapons complementing high-end missiles and sensors rather than replacing them.

Raytheon also is working on a modular weapons approach that combines existing components, including seekers, actuators and power systems. The goal is to shorten development cycles and respond more quickly to changing military needs.

International demand supports further expansion

About 48% of Raytheon’s backlog is international, up four percentage points from a year earlier. Calio said the company’s installed base and international production partnerships should help it compete as governments seek greater domestic involvement in weapons manufacturing.

He cited Patriot and NASAMS deployments across Europe and the Middle East, along with partnerships involving Kongsberg and MBDA. RTX also recently announced a Coyote co-production agreement with the United Arab Emirates.

The company has about 20,000 employees in Europe and is evaluating additional European suppliers for AMRAAM and Stinger. Calio said these arrangements can expand the supply base while strengthening relationships with foreign customers.

Commercial aftermarket outlook remains strong

On the commercial side, Calio said Boeing and Airbus both want to increase production. RTX expects to deliver a record number of geared turbofan engines this year and is investing to remain aligned with the aircraft manufacturers’ planned rate increases.

Although higher jet-fuel prices have pressured airlines, RTX has not seen a meaningful change in customer purchasing behavior, he said.

Calio pointed to a large pool of future maintenance work across the company’s installed engine base. About 15% of V2500 engines have not undergone their first shop visit and roughly half have not reached their second. At Pratt & Whitney Canada, about 60% of the installed base has yet to receive its first overhaul.

GTF maintenance output rose 40% from a year earlier in the second quarter, helping reduce aircraft-on-ground levels by 25% since the end of 2025. RTX has added seven GTF maintenance shops over the past three years, with newer locations reducing turnaround times for heavy shop visits by nearly 20%.

Cash conversion and margins offer upside

RTX continues to target a medium-term operating margin of 19% to 20% at Collins Aerospace. Calio identified commercial aftermarket growth, increased original-equipment production and structural cost reductions as the main drivers.

The company expects 2026 free cash flow of about $8.6 billion at the midpoint of its forecast. Calio declined to give a specific estimate for 2027, but said RTX’s longer-term fundamentals should support free cash flow equal to roughly 90% to 100% of adjusted net income.

RTX’s capital priorities remain investment in production capacity, debt reduction and dividends. Calio said the company expects debt to return to levels seen before its accelerated share-repurchase program by year-end. He also described the dividend as “sacrosanct,” signaling that shareholder payouts will remain a central part of the company’s capital-allocation strategy.

data.title: US FAA says billions more needed to modernize air traffic control
data.description:
By David Shepardson

The head of the Federal Aviation Administration said the first phase of an ambitious plan to modernize air traffic control will cost billions of dollars more than Congress has approved.

Last year, Congress approved $12.5 billion for air traffic control reforms, including $9 billion for air traffic modernization and $3.5 billion for facilities construction.

"It's costing $16 billion to do phase one," Bedford said at a U.S. House of Representatives subcommittee hearing. He said the FAA is funding the gap out of its facilities and equipment budget. The FAA wants at least another $10 billion for phase two of the project and Bedford urged lawmakers to approve it.

"The agency is working on scale-up to get this done and get it done right," Bedford said.

A Government Accountability Office report released on Tuesday said the FAA has underestimated the total costs of operating the new system or set a detailed schedule for completing reforms.

The GAO said the FAA has over 11,000 separate projects in phase one that it has previously estimated at $10.6 billion. Bedford said last year it wanted $15 billion or $16 billion for phase one, explaining the shortfall.

Congress approved the funding to address the aging air traffic control system, and boost controller hiring following decades of complaints over airport congestion and flight delays and a series of technology issues in recent years.

The price tag for telecommunications upgrades has jumped $4.75 billion to $5.91 billion, GAO said. Bedford said outdated telecom copper wires should be completely replaced by September 2027.

The FAA in December tapped Peraton, which is owned by Veritas Capital, to oversee the modernization effort, awarding it a $1.5 billion contract.

data.title: BL Explainer. Turmoil in Coforge
data.description:
Noida-based mid-tier information technology (IT) services firm Coforge is going through turmoil since the sudden announcement of its Chairperson O P Bhatt resigned abruptly from the company on September 8, after an internal audit raised concerns over the manner in which a ‘Board evaluation report’ was handled.

The share price has continued to decline, closing with 3.97 per cent decline at ₹1,774 on Tuesday, extending losses into a second week after the stock plunged nearly 9 per cent last on September 9, following the announcement of Bhatt’s resignation. An internal KPMG review found that his low evaluation rating had not been fully disclosed to the Board/ Nomination & Remuneration Committee.

The company immediately announced appointment of D K Singh, as the independent director and chair of the Nomination & Remuneration Committee, but in a fresh twist to the saga, the company on Friday said that Singh has also resigned, ‌citing “differences ⁠and tensions” ⁠between the firm’s independent and ​executive directors. The company said it has appointed Vivek Sharma as the Interim Chair and hired Egon Zehnder to identify two new independent directors.

What was the reason for these sudden resignations?

Both the resignations followed a KPMG internal audit that found gaps in how the Board’s evaluation scores had been reported. Coforge explained in a stock exchange filing that the internal audit found that Bhatt’s evaluation scores were shared with only Singh in his capacity as NRC chair, but were not passed on to the rest of the Board members.

Therefore, the remaining Directors sought explanations from the two because the underlying report was available only to them. However, the filing shared by the company also pushed back on any suggestion of discord within the Board and it described claims of tension between independent and Executive Directors as unfounded, adding that the allegation appeared to be an afterthought.

What did Coforge Board say after the resignations?

The management has told investors that these governance issues do not affect operations, financial reporting or FY27 strategy/ guidance. Brokerages including Jefferies and Emkay have also viewed the issue as largely a governance/conduct matter rather than an operational problem.

The company also held an investor/ analysts call for more than an hour on Monday (September 14) explaining the two resignations or the issues under considerations were not “personal”. “All of us hold our two transitional directors, who are no longer with the Board, in high regards and we wish them the very best,” Sudhir Singh, CEO and Executive Director said in his opening remarks of the call.

Encora Acquisition

During the concall, the company also said its guidance remains intact with outlook remaining robust whether in near, medium or long-term, despite the recent developments. Coforge expects its consolidated EBITDA margin of 20.5-21 per cent and EBIT margin of at least 15.5 per cent in the current fiscal year (FY27).

The company also said the recent developments have not changed its strategies or priorities and the new Board has also begun the process of strengthening its Independent Director pool. The company said the Encora acquisition was also becoming a major growth driver and the integration of Encora was one of Coforge’s biggest strategic moves. Its Q1 FY27 performance was also boosted substantially by the Encora acquisition, with revenue growing by around 49 per cent YoY, and the order book reaching a record $2.23 billion. Coforge management also expects the integration to support both growth and margin expansion, alongside cross-selling and AI capabilities.

What did the analysts says?

Jefferies, which maintains a Buy rating and a price target of Rs.2,040, characterised the Board’s explanation as reframing the issue. According to the brokerage firm, the clarification by Coforge suggests the matter is less about governance and more about the conduct of the departing directors, which should not impact the growth strategy of Coforge. According to Nuvama also, it sees no impact on financials due to the exits and it continues to rank Coforge as its top pick in the IT services sector.

Company says it has expanded automotive engineering footprint

Meanwhile, on Tuesday (September 15) Coforge also announced its expansion of automotive engineering footprint to accelerate connected, electric vehicle (EV) and software-defined vehicle innovation under the new Telecom, Media, Automotive, and Energy Solutions (TMAE) industry vertical.

Coforge’s automotive engineering practice now comprises around 300 professionals in Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, India, Europe and the US, with plans for further expansion, the company said in a filing. The expanded footprint will bring together engineering capabilities in mobility software, connectivity, cloud, cybersecurity, vehicle systems, and AI to support automotive companies as they navigate the transition toward increasingly software-defined and connected vehicles, it added.

data.title: Food inflation risks bolster case for commodities - WFII
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US equity indexes red; Dow leads losses down ~0.8%
  • Consumer Discretionary is weakest S&P 500 sector; energy leads gainers
  • Euro STOXX 600 index falls ~0.3%
  • Dollar gains; US crude up ~4%; gold slips; bitcoin falls >3%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.041%, highest since 2007, now ~5.0%

FOOD INFLATION RISKS BOLSTER CASE FOR COMMODITIES - WFII

Food inflation worries are adding support to the bullish commodity story, according to Wells Fargo Investment Institute's global real assets analyst, Mason Mendez.

In a recent note, Mendez says disruptions to global grain supplies and stubbornly high production costs are strengthening the case for commodities. Russia and Ukraine accounted for roughly 30% of global wheat exports in 2025, and attacks on grain terminals and shipping infrastructure in the Black Sea since July have raised fresh concerns about getting supplies to world markets.

Higher diesel, fertilizer and other farm-input costs are adding to the pressure. Those rising expenses have helped fuel a broad rally across agricultural markets, with most major ag commodities posting double-digit gains this year and wheat prices reaching their highest levels since 2022.

Mendez doesn't expect those pressures to ease anytime soon. The outlook for the Russia-Ukraine conflict remains uncertain, while refining-related challenges continue to keep production costs elevated.

Against that backdrop, WFII remains constructive on commodities. The firm sees broad commodity exposure as a potential hedge against further increases in food and energy prices and views pullbacks as buying opportunities. WFII expects the asset class to deliver further gains through 2027.

Meanwhile, the FTSE/Core Commodity CRB Total Return Index (.TRCCRBTR) finished Monday up nearly 46% so far this year.
